transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is voicing frustration with the United States,
saying that delays in delivering anti-ballistic missiles are costing Ukrainian lives.
And in an interview with the BBC, Zelensky also said he found it strange to see President Trump describe Vladimir Putin as a friend.
He was talking to the BBC's Sarah Rainsford in Kyiv.
I think Volodymyr Zelensky is navigating a very difficult relationship with the United States,
which is trying to mediate a peace process which Ukraine desperately needs,
but at the same time so often does seem to repeat lines coming from the Kremlin and not really understand Ukraine's position.
I think he accepts that Donald Trump wants to conclude a peace deal here in Ukraine,
and I think he believes that Donald Trump thinks the way to do that is through being friends with Vladimir Putin.
But I think he thinks that Donald Trump is deeply mistaken.
Speaking to reporters at Mar-a-Lago on Thanksgiving, President Trump again defended calling Putin a friend,
saying that he has to get a deal done to end Russia's war in Ukraine.
Democrats preparing to take power in Congress next year, the party united around the goal of expanding health coverage,
but lawmakers disagree about how to do it.
Here's NPR's Sam Greenglass.
The first step, says the next likely House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries,
is to reverse Republican cuts to Medicaid and restore enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies.
But we also know as Democrats that a return to the status quo is not acceptable.
Jeffries said this month he backs lowering the eligibility age for Medicare,
expanding it to cover vision, dental and hearing, and guaranteeing universal coverage for children.
Some Democrats are unsure, others say reform needs to go further,
and want to advance single-payer insurance or Medicare for all.
Because President Trump may be unwilling to sign any of this,
debates now over healthcare could shape the direction Democrats go in the 2028 presidential campaign.
Sam Greenglass, NPR News, Washington.
Government figures show fewer people from outside Europe migrating into the UK,
as well as asylum requests dropping by a third over the past year ending in September.
Overall, net migration has dropped to its lowest level since 1997, excluding the pandemic,
down about 90 percent from 2023.
This could weaken support for far-right lawmaker Nigel Farage's anti-immigrant party,
which has already been slumping in the polls amid corruption allegations.
Successive British governments on both the right and left have tightened immigration rules
for workers and students, and restricted the ways people can claim asylum.
But reduced immigration could potentially hinder the British economy
by shrinking the workforce and straining public finances.
Lauren Fryer, NPR News, London.
Coastal flooding has affected areas from North Carolina to New York.
California has also faced coastal flooding.
U.S. Environmental Protection Agency says it expects test results from samples taken
after Wednesday's controlled detonation of degraded bomb-making material in Iowa to come in soon.
The EPA says results could come as soon as today.
The agency says it took more than 1,500 samples of air, water, soil and dust
before the detonation and hundreds after it.
Hundreds gathered Thursday morning for the annual sunrise ceremony on Alcatraz Island
in the middle of the San Francisco Bay,
commemorating the indigenous occupation of Alcatraz.
Lakshmi Sarah of member station KQED reports.
Attendees crowded around a bonfire before sunrise for a series of dances, songs and speeches,
including speakers who were veterans of the indigenous occupation of Alcatraz in 1969.
Chokee Cottier is the daughter of Belva Cottier,
the woman who first proposed the idea of occupation to reclaim land
and challenge the government's treatment of Native American people.
Alcatraz sparked indigenous flames around the world to become bonfires.
It's time to do that again, from our grassroots to the very top.
The occupation helped inspire a nationwide indigenous political movement,
something organizers advocated for. Fran PR News.
This message comes from Rosetta Stone.
Rosetta Stone is designed to make language learning intuitive.
It mimics how people naturally acquire speech as children,
helping users read, write and think in a second language.
More at RosettaStone.com.

Trump defends calling Putin a friend, saying a deal is needed to end Ukraine war
Democrats in Congress split on how to expand health coverage after reversing Republican Medicaid cuts
UK net migration falls to lowest level since 1997, asylum requests drop by a third
Coastal flooding affects areas from North Carolina to New York and California
EPA awaits test results after controlled detonation of bomb-making material in Iowa
Hundreds attend sunrise ceremony on Alcatraz marking the 1969 indigenous occupation
